label: first input token is digit 2
explanation: Fires only at step t=0 when the input token is the digit 2, i.e. the first original token of the sequence is 2. Magnitude is constant (1.156) on every activation, so nothing modulates it. It does not fire on 2 at any later position, on any other first token, or in the delimiter or copy phases. On the dev split it fires on exactly the steps the predicate picks out (P=R=1).

issues: No refutation found. Test split: P=R=F1=mass recall=1.0 (16538 active steps, 16538 predicted). Misses on test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.
Profile confirms every activation is at t=0 in the original phase, none in the delimiter or copy phases, and the magnitude is constant (mean = median = max = 1.156).
The 'never on later 2s' claim checks out: in_tok==2 alone has recall 1.0 but precision 0.084, so later 2s do not fire it. The predicate (t>0) has recall 0.
The by-L distribution is flat in absolute counts. Its rate varies only because longer sequences have more steps, so there is no length dependence. The label does not overclaim.
